This legislation ensures that the Department of Defense is able to leverage rapidly advancing artificial intelligence technology to respond to these kinds of cyber-attacks and keep pace with the capabilities of our geo-political rivals. AI is increasingly central to modern, strategic warfare, and the United States needs to be prepared with a robust digital defense to meet these evolving national security challenges.

The third place winners of the 2025 Congressional App Challenge from California’s 19th Congressional District are Bryan Hu and Jun Jiang from Valley Christian High School for creating their app, “Billion.” Billion uses AI to analyze complex government websites and documents to synthesize them into condensed, user-friendly summaries. Their app helps users stay informed on changes in the government and political development enables us to engage with our democratic process. I’m proud of Bryan and Jun for their work and look forward to their continued success!

I’m proud to announce that the 2025 first place winner of the Congressional App Challenge for California’s 19th Congressional District is Saumit Pathak from Silver Creek High School. Saumit created his innovative app, “LeftoSense,” which uses AI to address food safety and encourage food donations. The app evaluates food safety for consumption and then directs users to the nearest food donation point through Google Maps. By creating this app, Saumit helps users reduce waste, stay healthy, and empowers them to address local issues of food insecurity. Congratulations to Saumit for honing his talent to make a real impact in our community.

The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) technology comes with serious risks. If the world continues to adopt AI at a rapid rate without greater safety controls and slower development, incidents could threaten our security and safety. As leading artificial intelligence companies voice their concerns on the dangers that AI presents, Congress must act proactively to ensure proper guardrails are put in place to protect our country and humanity and ensure that AI deployment is safe, stable, and secure.

Unfortunately, President Donald Trump refuses to lead on this issue and Speaker of the House Mike Johnson blocked a bipartisan AI task force that would address the same concerns being raised by AI CEOs. The United States Congress must take decisive action now to slow AI development by coordinating both across the aisle and with our global partners to set strong safety standards and guardrails for this technology while preserving American innovation and competitiveness. 
 
Although Congress is working on solutions, we must do more to ensure that the necessary conversations are taking place so that safeguards and standards can be put in place to protect us. I do believe that AI can improve the quality of our lives. However, the benefits of AI will only outweigh its potential threats if we take the deliberate time and care to ensure responsible AI development and to get it right.

Congress has a responsibility to act when it comes to AI. That’s why I joined @RepLiccardo and over 100 of my colleagues in calling on Speaker Johnson to keep the House in session so that we can vote on AI safeguards. https://t.co/13pMzBHGQu

The AI boom has significant potential but creates serious new threats. Leadership must be shown at all levels of government to implement guardrails that ensure that AI deployment is safe, stable, and secure. 

https://t.co/cL79dXlJ2P

As emerging AI reshapes our education system and workforce, the federal government needs to step up with guardrails and programs to protect our students, teachers, and working families. I’m proud to support the Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act, which would create enforceable safeguards and invest in professional development programs to empower students and working families while ensuring AI is deployed responsibly.

As the emergence of artificial intelligence reshapes our education system and workforce, the federal government needs to lead with the appropriate guardrails and necessary programs to protect our students, teachers, and working families. I'm proud to cosponsor this wide-ranging federal framework to ensure that AI is deployed strategically in classrooms and offices, protecting human-centered education and training, while investing in open-access research, upskilling resources, new pilot programs, clear safety standards, and transparency. AI has significant potential, but we must implement standards to ensure its deployment is safe, stable, and secure.

As the U.S. works to maintain its competitive edge when it comes to AI, we also must lead on establishing clear global AI standards and security, starting with China. That’s why I joined a bipartisan group urging the President to strengthen AI testing, reporting, and international coordination to bolster our technological leadership while protecting our national security.
